extracted.intended_audience: Goodwill ~ Redwood Empire staff, marketing and communications personnel
extracted.subtask_description: Brand and writing guidelines for Goodwill ~ Redwood Empire staff who produce external and internal communications (logos, print, e-mail, letters, templates, and marketing materials). Provides visual identity rules and editorial/formatting standards to ensure consistent, professional messaging.

rubrics_metrics.name: Brand consistency and professionalism
rubrics_metrics.description: These brand guidelines are provided to remain consistent and to enhance the professionalism of Goodwill ~ Redwood Empire (GIRE) by ensuring we use the correct brand identity standards while communicating in the most professional way possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use correct visual and verbal identity elements (brand mark, typography, color palette, templates, writing standards) so community members, donors and partners experience the brand consistently; accurate implementation protects brand equity and supports organizational value.

rubrics_metrics.name: Logo usage — versions and color options
rubrics_metrics.description: Created in 1968, the “Smiling G” trademark is the Goodwill logo. The preferred color of the logo is the version using Pantone Reflex Blue and Black. When needed, there are four options available for reproduction purposes: two-color (Black with Reflex Blue), one-color (Black), alternative one-color (Reflex Blue), and reverse use (White on solid background).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the two-color preferred version when possible. Alternative versions (black, reflex blue, white reverse) are allowed for reproduction constraints. Follow reproduction options to maintain brand recognition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Logo integrity — proportion, typeface, sizing, spacing, and trademark mark
rubrics_metrics.description: At no time will the logo be changed in proportions – that is, stretched or compressed. At no time may the typeface in the logo be changed. The integrity of the logo must be maintained at all times.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not alter proportions or change the logo typeface. Minimum logo size: 0.25” wide to maintain legibility; no upper limit if proportionate. Provide ample clear space around the Smiling G ('room to breathe'). The registered trademark symbol should always be in the lower right corner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Registered word mark usage
rubrics_metrics.description: Goodwill is a registered trademark both as a logo and as a word mark.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Three rules: Proper use of Goodwill Industries: Goodwill Industries®; Proper use of Goodwill alone: Goodwill®; Use the registration symbol for the word mark the first time the term is mentioned in a document.

rubrics_metrics.name: Localized and co-branded logo use
rubrics_metrics.description: The localized GIRE logo should be used whenever possible in materials and should follow similar guidelines as outlined above.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Donate Movement logo preferred with 'Powered by Goodwill' directly beneath it. If using the Donate Movement logo without 'Powered by Goodwill,' place the Smiling G logo in close proximity for better brand recognition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Color palette and color codes
rubrics_metrics.description: The primary brand colors of Goodwill are Reflex Blue and Black. GIRE has expanded the color palette to include colors found on trucks, CDC containers and stores.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Primary and additional color swatches are specified with CMYK, RGB, HEX and Pantone codes (e.g., Reflex Blue: C:100 M:73 Y:0 K:2, R:0 G:85 B:164, #0055A4). Use the specified color codes for consistent reproduction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Typography — primary and secondary typefaces and uses
rubrics_metrics.description: The Helvetica type family is the primary font for Goodwill. The secondary font for Goodwill is Times New Roman. All weights of Helvetica are acceptable for Goodwill’s communications. All weights of Times New Roman may be used as long as they are not the primary typeface in a document.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Helvetica or Helvetica Neue for headlines; if Helvetica is unavailable, acceptable headline alternatives are Arial and Century Gothic. Use Arial for body copy in correspondence, publications, PowerPoint, and website narrative text. Times New Roman and Garamond may be used for body text (not for headlines/subheadings); italics may be used for quotes. Follow specified weights and do not use serif fonts for headlines.

rubrics_metrics.name: E-mail composition and conduct
rubrics_metrics.description: Although considered to be the most informal written communication available, e-mails still reflect on GIRE and our professionalism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Always include a brief subject line; ensure e-mails are grammatically correct, brief and to the point. E-mails are required to be sent from the agency server (e.g., abc@gire.org) and not from personal accounts. E-mails are not confidential. Use the correct e-mail signature. Consider three-sets-of-eyes for formal external messages.

rubrics_metrics.name: E-mail signature content and formatting
rubrics_metrics.description: Please make sure your email signatures are set-up as follows: (example signature block provided). New e-mail signature formatting: Name = Garamond, 12, Bold, Black; Title = Garamond, 12, Black; Agency Name = Garamond, 12, Blue; Address, Phone, Fax = Garamond, 10, Black; Mission Statement = Garamond, 14, Italic, Blue; Confidentiality Statement = Times New Roman, 10, Black.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include contact details, agency name and the mission statement line. Include the confidentiality notice text as provided. Hyperlink icons to specified URLs (Smiling G, Facebook, LinkedIn, Google+, YouTube). Reply e-mail signature formatting: all Arial, 10, black except agency name in blue. You may copy icon code from a co-worker but update personal details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Microsoft Outlook signature setup procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: Instructions for changing your Microsoft Outlook e-mail signatures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Set message format to HTML. Ensure stationery default is <None>. Use Signatures > Create Signatures > New to create new signatures for new and reply e-mails, type contact info into preview pane, click OK, then Apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Three-sets-of-eyes proofreading requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The three-sets-of-eyes requirement (including eyes from the marketing department) may apply to e-mail messages sent outside the office, particularly if they are formal announcements, invitations, or contain substantial content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Before release, have two additional people (including one from marketing) proofread materials in addition to the originator. Adjust work schedules to allow time for these reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grammar, punctuation, and general formatting rules
rubrics_metrics.description: How we use language is important. Subjects and verbs must agree. We must write so people understand what we are saying. Keep sentences short and to the point.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not underline copy for emphasis; use italics or bold sparingly. Do not double-space after periods. Use 'c:' instead of 'cc:' when copying others. Spell-check every document but also proofread (spell-check does not replace proofreading). Use exclamation points sparingly. Use hyphens for compound words or line breaks; use the en dash (–), not the hyphen (-), between thoughts. Watch for widows and orphans; prefer left-aligned (ragged right) text rather than fully justified to avoid distracting spacing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title capitalization rules
rubrics_metrics.description: The first word and all the main words in a title should have initial capitals, and all the ‘joining’ words should be left in lower case.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Always capitalize the first and last word and major words such as nouns, pronouns, verbs, and modifiers (adverbs, adjectives, subordinating conjunctions, hyphenated compounds, and the first word after a colon). Do not capitalize articles (a, an, the), coordinating conjunctions (and, but, or, nor, so), 'to' before an infinitive, or prepositions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Letter formatting standards
rubrics_metrics.description: When preparing letters, please note the following: All letters are to be composed using Times New Roman regular 12-point type.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Date is four spaces down from the name/address block; recipient’s name/address block two spaces down from the date; greeting double-spaced from recipient block (use colon for formal greeting, comma for informal); body starts two spaces below greeting. Paragraphs flush left, ragged right, with a double-space between paragraphs. Double-space before the closing and allow room for a handwritten signature, followed by typed name and title. For copies, double-space below signer’s title and use 'c:' followed by names.

rubrics_metrics.name: Templates and asset locations
rubrics_metrics.description: Templates and logos are stored on the server.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Microsoft Word and PowerPoint templates: P:\GIRE\Master Forms. Logos (GIRE and Smiling G): P:\GIRE\Marketing. Use these templates and assets whenever possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Writing clarity and plain-language expectation
rubrics_metrics.description: We must write so people understand what we are saying. We need to keep our sentences short and to the point.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure subject-verb agreement, prefer short sentences, avoid unnecessary jargon; format and proofread to ensure clarity and readability for the audience.

rubrics_metrics.name: FAQ and donor-facing content guidance (tone and message)
rubrics_metrics.description: FAQ content communicates organizational purpose and differences (e.g., why donate to Goodwill vs other thrift stores) and explains programmatic variation by community need.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When drafting donor/shopper-facing content, emphasize mission-driven impact (employment and training), clarity about fundraising models, and local program tailoring. Use positive messaging to reassure donors (e.g., shopping does not deprive disadvantaged people).
